items.title: EUMAM MOZ supports Lar Nossa Senhora dos Desamparados with essential supplies
items.summary: The initiative was attended by the EUMAM MOZ Force Commander, Brigadier General Sérgio Estrela, who, accompanied by Mission personnel, visited both the female and male residential wards of the care home. items.title: South Africa's ANC facing worst-ever performance in local elections
items.summary: Near-final results show South Africa's once dominant ANC will see its lowest-ever vote percentage. The party is taking the blame for shoddy municipal services, including water and electricity shortages South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) is heading for an historically poor election performance , with the near-final tally from Wednesday's municipal polls showing it coming in with just over 30% of the vote The ANC also lost its majority in six of the eight metropolitan regions, South Africa's Electoral Commission said Saturday in sharing the results after 98% of votes were counted South African voters in 2026 are angry about water and electricity shortages, with the ANC taking the blame for the poor state of municipalities. High unemployment, crime, and widespread corruption are other pressing issues ANC leader, and South African president, Cyril Ramaphosa , has not yet addressed the poor performance as of Saturday evening.

items.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
items.summary: The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated " following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases…

items.title: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
items.summary: New Zealand election 'too close to call' - so who's won? There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36 seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the "shape of the next government" will remain uncertain "for a while" The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36.

items.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a political crisis and a standoff between the presidency and judiciary Thursday's ruling came a day after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed - a move which the court said the president lacked the authority to take The court also ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, potentially disrupting government plans for nationwide polls next year Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May, but his administration extended it by a year through law changes approved by parliament in March Opposition groups accuse him of using the constitutional changes to prolong his rule But the president insists the reforms are necessary to move Somalia towards fully democratic elections, replacing the clan-based system in which elders pick their representatives which has been used since 2012 Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 and has…
